words.sense: official collective pardon for past offenses
misconceptions: Any individual sentence reduction is a collective pardon

words.sense: merciful reduction or easing of a penalty
misconceptions: A group pardon must be the same as individual leniency

semantic_axes.description: A broad pardon for a group differs from mercy that lessens an existing penalty.

edges.boundary_rule: amnesty wipes away punishment for a group of past offenses; clemency mercifully eases a penalty.

misconceptions.M1: Thinks any act of mercy is a general pardon
misconceptions.M2: Thinks an entire group pardon is just an individual sentence change
misconceptions.M3: Confuses public sympathy with the legal scope of relief

chains.frame: Which word best describes the government decision Amina read about?

beats.text: Amina read that officials wiped out the penalties for every participant in last year’s banned demonstration.
beats.decisive_clue: official pardon covered a whole group
beats.reason: Collective relief for past offenses is the defining fact.

beats.text: The decision was announced on television after a long debate.
beats.decisive_clue: groupwide forgiveness despite a public announcement
beats.reason: Publicity does not make this an individual penalty reduction.

chains.feedback_short: Key evidence: groupwide forgiveness despite a public announcement.
chains.feedback_deep: amnesty means an official pardon granted to a defined group for earlier offenses; clemency means mercy that reduces or softens a punishment, often for an individual. Collective relief for past offenses is the defining fact. Publicity does not make this an individual penalty reduction.
chains.contrast_rule: amnesty wipes away punishment for a group of past offenses; clemency mercifully eases a penalty.
